saturation.assessment: A universal saturated/not-saturated label is not established for family medicine. Local paid demand and service design need separate assessment.

For a CHC/secondary-care role, verify staffing, emergency backup, referral links and the exact procedures expected.
Check whether salaried employment permits outside clinic work, and model follow-up time and overheads before investing.

other_routes.name: Broad pediatric practice with selective referral
other_routes.description: General pediatrics, development, prevention and newborn care are part of the core curriculum. A specialist referral network and appropriate level-of-care limits matter more than presenting every possible course as compulsory.

saturation.assessment: A universal saturated/not-saturated label is not established for paediatrics. Evaluate the location, funded role, skill mix and service model.
saturation.evidence_limits: Curricula and admissions data are not measured local job demand, hiring competition or take-home income. Added training seats and patient need do not establish funded vacancies or a profitable independent service.
practical_checks: Separate broad pediatric posts from NICU/PICU or organ-specialty posts requiring specific advanced training and experience.
Assess births, child/adolescent population, referral catchment, payer mix and existing service capacity; a disease-need story is not a job offer.
For hospital work, verify night rota, nursing ratios, neonatal/pediatric equipment and access to specialist/transport backup.
For a focused fellowship, verify personal supervised cases, outcomes review, recognition and how recent graduates were hired.
Model vaccination, consultation and inpatient receipts separately from salaries and net owner profit.

branches.overview: MD/DNB Biochemistry is a diagnostic, quality, teaching and research pathway rather than merely a classroom subject. after_md_ms.setting: Medical college or teaching hospital
after_md_ms.description: Teach biochemical concepts and laboratory interpretation to medical and allied-health learners, build supervised service competence and pursue academic recruitment subject to current eligibility rules.

salary_methodology: Each row is one dated policy, institutional notice or advertised role, not an all-India salary survey. Offers and actual payments have not been independently confirmed.

All amounts are INR. Monthly pay, annual remuneration, pay-matrix basic, consolidated pay and training stipends retain their original units and basis. Annual divided by 12 is only a monthly equivalent, never take-home pay.

Government basic pay excludes applicable NPA/DA/HRA and deductions unless the source explicitly states otherwise. A pay-band maximum is not an entry salary. Stipends are paid during training, not after qualification.

Tier 1 is an editorial comparison group: Delhi-NCR, Mumbai metro, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Pune and Ahmedabad. Tier 2 names secondary urban centres explicitly; smaller towns, districts, multiple locations and national policies are separately labelled. These are not official HRA X/Y/Z categories.

Missing pay remains null, never zero. Negotiable roles and contradictory portal fields are labelled. A recruiter listing does not establish a funded vacancy, current availability, a named corporate employer or average realised pay.

Salary stages follow explicit qualifications and experience in the source. Fresh MD, fellow, DM/DrNB trainee and post-SS consultant are different stages; no fixed fellowship premium or guaranteed increment is inferred.
Private practice receipts, hospital billings and procedure fees are revenue, not personal earnings. Rent, staff, equipment, finance, consumables, taxes, collection delays and referral ethics matter.

Corporate-chain salary tables by branch, city and experience are not consistently public. Named-chain examples are shown where available; unidentified clients and missing offers remain evidence gaps. No salary league table is constructed from this convenience sample.
Saturation is assessed as a local employment and referral problem. Seat counts, portal listing counts and podcast anecdotes cannot measure unemployment or prove a national surplus of specialists.

sections.title: Use earnings evidence at the right career stage
points: Immediately after MD/MS: compare supervised senior-resident and junior-consultant posts with actual duty hours, on-call nights and the skills you still need. Fresh qualification does not guarantee independent procedural readiness or a faculty appointment.

During fellowship or DM/MCh/DrNB: calculate living costs, tuition, stipend, examination costs, any bond and foregone salary. A three-year training period can be financially worthwhile without increasing income immediately on graduation.

First focused or superspecialist post: ask whether the advertised role actually uses your new skill, how much independent work you receive and what backup exists. A certificate alone does not demonstrate employability or grant universal privileges.

Established consultant: separate fixed salary, variable incentives, professional fees and business profits. Department leadership and an ethical referral network can matter more than another short certificate. No uniform year-by-year salary ladder is established by these sources.

Government careers: distinguish regular cadre posts, tenure senior residency, contract faculty and project appointments. Entry qualifications, experience, recruitment rules and benefits differ; a pay-band ceiling is not your starting basic pay.

Industry and research careers: compare the actual role and required skills, such as medical affairs, pharmacovigilance, trials, diagnostics or research. A job titled pharmacologist or biochemist may accept non-medical graduates; it is not automatically an MD salary comparator.

sections.title: Tier 1 versus Tier 2: compare the whole offer
points: Do not assume a metro always pays more. A smaller-city offer may compensate for relocation, language needs, emergency cover or lack of specialist backup. This research sample cannot estimate a causal city premium.

Use two or three named cities you would realistically live in. For each branch, collect at least three current written offers with the same qualification, experience, duty hours and fixed-versus-variable pay definition before deciding on a likely earnings range.

For Tier 1, investigate whether the hospital already has established consultants, who controls referrals, whether new consultants receive cases and whether a subspecialist can build a sustainable niche.

For Tier 2, verify local paying demand, referral catchment, case mix, equipment downtime, ICU and anaesthesia support, competing services and the ability to refer complex cases safely. Unmet health need alone does not prove a funded job.

Compare monthly fixed pay after known deductions with rent, commute, childcare, night duties, professional indemnity and relocation costs. Do not estimate take-home from basic pay without the employer's allowance and deduction breakdown.

sections.title: A practical saturation audit
points: Treat saturation as a branch-by-city-by-role question. Competition for an academic post, a salaried corporate post, surgical case access and a new clinic are different markets.

Ask recent graduates from at least three institutions where they actually joined, how long the search took, whether the post uses their training and what the fixed written offer was. Include ordinary graduates, not only star alumni.
Check referral concentration and training quality: an oversupplied generalist market may still reward a demonstrable skill gap, but another fellowship has costs and no guaranteed premium.
Compare job turnover and repeated adverts with funded filled posts. A long list of portal adverts can contain duplicates, old roles and unnamed clients; it is not a workforce shortage estimate.

National specialist unemployment, matched salary distributions and an all-city saturation index were not established here. Interview warnings remain attributed perspectives in the video and Conclusions pages.

sections.title: Questions to ask a private hospital or corporate chain
points: What is the guaranteed fixed monthly amount? Is the figure gross salary, annual CTC, professional retainer or expected total including incentives? Ask for the exact written breakup.

What counts toward incentives, who owns collections, when are they paid and can the employer change the formula? Ask about refunds, revenue thresholds, exclusivity, notice period and restrictive clauses.
How many consultants share the cases and on-call roster? Ask for actual recent OPD, admission and procedure volumes and the allocation method, with patient confidentiality protected.
For procedures and diagnostics, who pays for equipment, consumables, staff, reporting software and indemnity? Confirm the clinical privileges and supervision attached to the post.

For a fellowship, request a written rotation plan, supervised and independent case targets, faculty availability, assessment method, fees, stipend and recent alumni destinations. Marketing language is not a placement guarantee.
